text: Please describe how you have learned about and engaged with Tufts during your college search process.
applies_to: all applicants

text: Tell us about one of your favorite school assignments in the past two years. What was the assignment and why did you enjoy it?
applies_to: School of Arts and Sciences applicants only

text: Write a short thank-you note to someone you have not yet thanked and would like to acknowledge. (We encourage you to share this note with that person, if possible, and reflect on the experience!)
applies_to: all applicants (first-year and transfer)

text: How will you explore community at Penn? Consider how Penn will help shape your perspective, and how your experiences and perspective will help shape Penn.
applies_to: all applicants (first-year and transfer)

text: The College of Arts and Sciences is designed to foster discovery and connection. Describe something you are curious about—something you'd like to learn more about or find a new approach to—and how you might pursue that curiosity in the College.
applies_to: College of Arts and Sciences single-degree applicants (including dual-degree/specialized program applicants whose single-degree choice is the College)

text: Please explain what draws you to the academic areas you selected above and how you hope to explore them at Rice University.
applies_to: all first-year applicants (domestic, international, QuestBridge)

text: Based upon your exploration of Rice University, what elements of the Rice experience appeal to you?
applies_to: all first-year applicants (domestic, international, QuestBridge)

text: The Residential College System is at the heart of Rice student life and is heavily influenced by the particular cultural traditions and unique life experiences each student brings. What life experiences and/or unique perspectives are you looking forward to sharing with fellow Owls in the residential college system?
applies_to: all first-year applicants; optional for QuestBridge applicants

text: Rice is strengthened by its diverse community of learning and discovery that produces leaders and change agents across the spectrum of human endeavor. What perspectives shaped by your background, experiences, upbringing, and/or cultural identity inspire you to join our community of change agents at Rice?
applies_to: all first-year applicants; optional for QuestBridge applicants

text: What academic areas are you interested in exploring at Emory University and why?
applies_to: all first-year applicants (Emory College, Oxford College, or both)

text: Emory University has a strong commitment to building community. Tell us about a community that you have been part of where your personal participation helped to change or shape the community for the better.
applies_to: all first-year applicants (Emory College, Oxford College, or both); answer one of the four 'Getting to Know You' questions

text: Reflect on a personal experience where you intentionally expanded your cultural awareness.
applies_to: all first-year applicants (Emory College, Oxford College, or both); answer one of the four 'Getting to Know You' questions

text: Emory University’s unique mission calls for service to humanity. Share how you might personally contribute to this mission of service to humanity.
applies_to: all first-year applicants (Emory College, Oxford College, or both); answer one of the four 'Getting to Know You' questions

text: In a scholarly community, differing ideas often collide before they converge. How do you personally navigate disagreement in a way that promotes progress and deepens meaningful dialogue?
applies_to: all first-year applicants (Emory College, Oxford College, or both); answer one of the four 'Getting to Know You' questions

text: Strong communities are sustained by traditions. Boston College's annual calendar is marked with both long-standing and newer traditions that help shape our community. Tell us about a meaningful tradition in your family or community. Why is it important to you, and how does it bring people together or strengthen the bonds of those who participate?
applies_to: all applicants except Human-Centered Engineering (HCE) major applicants

text: The late BC theology professor, Father Michael Himes, argued that a university is not a place to which you go, but instead, a "rigorous and sustained conversation about the great questions of human existence, among the widest possible circle of the best possible conversation partners.” Who has been your most meaningful conversation partner, and what profound questions have you considered together?
applies_to: all applicants except Human-Centered Engineering (HCE) major applicants

text: In her July 2009 Ted Talk, “The Danger of a Single Story,” Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie warned viewers against assigning people a “single story” through assumptions about their nationality, appearance, or background. Discuss a time when someone defined you by a single story. What challenges did this present and how did you overcome them?
applies_to: all applicants except Human-Centered Engineering (HCE) major applicants

text: Boston College’s Jesuit mission highlights “the three Be’s”: be attentive, be reflective, be loving – core to Jesuit education (see A Pocket Guide to Jesuit Education). If you could add a fourth “Be,” what would it be and why? How would this new value support your personal development and enrich the BC community?
applies_to: all applicants except Human-Centered Engineering (HCE) major applicants

text: What about being a student at BU most excites you?
applies_to: all first-year applicants (Common App)

text: As Pope Leo XIV (Villanova Class of 1977) has said, “no one can single-handedly bear the weight of the challenges the world is facing, just as no one is so weak that they cannot play their part.” What have you done to play your part in advancing equity and justice in your community?
applies_to: all first-year applicants (Common App or Coalition App)

text: What is a lesson in life that you have learned that you would want to share with others at Villanova?
applies_to: all first-year applicants (Common App or Coalition App)

text: "Villanova" means "new home." Why do you want to call Villanova your new home?
applies_to: all first-year applicants (Common App or Coalition App)

text: Villanova embraces Artificial Intelligence (AI) with a commitment to thoughtful, ethical use rooted in our Augustinian mission and values. How do you see technology helping you to lead, serve, and contribute to the common good?
applies_to: all first-year applicants (Common App or Coalition App)

text: At Villanova, we often say "each of us strengthens all of us." Please detail a time when someone has borrowed some of your strength in their time of need.
applies_to: all first-year applicants (Common App or Coalition App)

text: At Fordham, we expect students to care for and engage with their communities and be active citizens for positive change. Please share an experience you had that caused you to develop a new perspective, change your point of view, and/or empower you to take an action or be courageous. Your response should include examples of your personal growth (e.g., what did you learn, did your point of view change, did you develop new skills or strengths?).
applies_to: all applicants (optional short response; choose one of three)

text: Our motto is “New York is my campus, Fordham is my school.” New York City is a diverse and global city that provides Fordham students with a special kind of educational experience, full of both challenge and opportunity. What has prepared you to embrace the unique opportunity of living and learning in New York City?
applies_to: all applicants (optional short response; choose one of three)

text: At Fordham, we have a tradition of having our graduating seniors send a message to their younger selves. What will the future “you” tell the “you” of today about what you accomplished as a Fordham student?
applies_to: all applicants (optional short response; choose one of three)

text: Please tell us why you want to attend UMass Amherst?
applies_to: all applicants

text: Please tell us why you chose the Major(s) you did.
applies_to: all applicants

text: At UMass Amherst, no two students are alike. Our communities and groups often define us and shape our individual worlds. Community can refer to various aspects, including shared geography, religion, race/ethnicity, income, ideology, and more. Please choose one of your communities or groups and describe its significance. Explain how, as a product of this community or group, you would enrich our campus.
applies_to: Applicants not interested in Commonwealth Honors College
